[raw subtype: tumoral] c: Clinical photograph showing the verrucous form of chromoblastomycosis, explicitly identified as panel (c); the caption specifically notes black dots in the lesions. [raw subtype: verrucous] d: Clinical photograph of a plaque form of chromoblastomycosis, explicitly identified as panel (d) in the caption. [raw subtype: plaque] e: Clinical photograph showing the cicatricial form of chromoblastomycosis, explicitly identified as panel (e), with a prominent pale scar-like lesion. in_text_mentions: CBM exhibits five different clinical forms: nodular, tumoral type, verrucous, plaque, and cicatricial (Figure 6). In the nodular form, fairly soft, pale pink or purple, small nodules can be identified, and the surface of the nodules may be smooth, papillary, or scaly. If not properly treated, these nodules can gradually develop into the tumoral form of the CBM. In the tumoral form, the lesions are larger and more protruding, papillomatous, or lobulated than in the nodular form and can exhibit tumor-like masses.
